title: feat(mouseutils): add haptic feedback to Cursor Wrap

proposed_comments.title: Avoid intercepting edge input when no wrap is pending
proposed_comments.body:
### Avoid intercepting edge input when no wrap is pending

**Severity:** `medium` - potential interference with ordinary edge input when a haptic device is present.

`RegisterHapticEdgeWindows()` shows four topmost layered popup windows spanning the virtual-screen edges for the entire hook lifetime. Their alpha is 1 rather than zero, and they have no input-transparent style or hit-test handling. They can therefore become the input target instead of the application or shell below, including while modifier-gated wrapping is inactive.

Please ensure that the haptic input windows cannot intercept ordinary non-wrap input. A window shown only while completing an actual wrap is one option, but the behavioral requirement does not mandate that particular redesign. Any temporary input window should be hidden or removed when the wrap completes, is cancelled, or the hook stops.

Verify ordinary movement and clicks along each edge reach the underlying application or shell while no wrap is requested, especially with Ctrl/Shift activation configured but not held. Then verify actual wrapping still produces haptic feedback on supported hardware.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve deferred-wrap completion and refresh stale haptic routing
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This coordinates the deferred completion, display/device notification and hook-lifecycle paths in the same file; a single inline replacement would not express the complete behavioral correction.
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve deferred-wrap completion and refresh stale haptic routing

**Severity:** `medium` - deferred completion risk; startup-only haptic availability is a lower-impact optional-feedback limitation.

**Affected code:** `src/modules/MouseUtils/CursorWrap/dllmain.cpp`: `InitializeHaptics`, `OnDisplayChange`, `RegisterHapticEdgeWindows`, `TryDeferWrapToHapticEdgeWindow`, `CompletePendingHapticWrap` and hook shutdown.

**Problem:** Haptic availability is sampled only when the listener starts, and `OnDisplayChange()` updates monitor information without refreshing the existing edge windows. Separately, once `TryDeferWrapToHapticEdgeWindow()` accepts a wrap, completion relies exclusively on a later `WM_MOUSEMOVE` reaching an edge window; there is no alternate completion path if that delivery does not occur.

**Why it matters:** Device or topology changes can leave optional haptic feedback unavailable or windows positioned at old virtual-screen edges. If an accepted deferred message is not delivered, that particular cursor transition has no guaranteed completion. The latter is a code-path risk, not a reproduced permanent hang. A failed hit test or unavailable haptic route already falls back to direct `SetCursorPos`, so those cases do not by themselves establish that wrapping stops. `m_hasPendingWrap` also does not globally block later hook processing.

**Suggested change:**
1. Refresh or invalidate haptic availability and window geometry through the existing device/display lifecycle, preserving the direct-wrap fallback when haptics cannot be used.
2. Give every accepted deferred wrap a bounded completion or safe cancellation path if its expected message never arrives; a timeout is one option rather than a required architecture.
3. Clear stale pending destinations and temporary input-window state on topology changes and hook teardown. Keep this coordinated with the non-wrap input-interception correction.

**Verification:** On supported hardware, change display topology and reconnect the haptic device while active; verify optional feedback recovers or safely falls back. Exercise staggered monitor layouts and window-creation failure to confirm direct wrapping still works. Suppress the expected deferred mouse message in a controlled check and verify a deferred transition cannot remain pending indefinitely.
